Fixtures use a fictional acme/widgets repo.

evals.expected_output: Correct worktrees off origin/main, a launcher with the absolute claude path, a wt command with an existing profile, briefs that carry the skill's required elements, a migration number taken from the directory, and an exclude list covering every file written into a worktree.
expectations: Runs `git fetch origin` and fast-forwards local main, then creates each worktree with `git worktree add -b <branch>` from origin/main at a short path ending issue-65 / issue-67.

The wt commands use `-w 0 new-tab`, `-d <worktree>`, a `--title`, and `cmd /c <worktree>\claude-start.cmd`, with a `-p` profile that exists in the settings output (PowerShell, Command Prompt or Ubuntu), not 'Windows PowerShell'.
Each claude-start.cmd calls claude by its absolute path (C:\Users\dev\.local\bin\claude.exe, because `cmd /c where claude` fails) and contains no semicolon.
The issue-65 brief takes the migration number from the migrations directory (0015), not the issue body's 0013.
Each brief names the other session and what it owns / must not touch (issue-67 must not touch exporter/; issue-65 must not touch docs/api.md or docs/export.md).
Both briefs say: integrate by MERGE not rebase (repo history is merge-based), do not merge your own PR, report the head SHA when you push, do not open new issues, and derive counts at the tree.
Each brief carries the machine constraint that applies to its session: one test suite at a time on this machine and, for the session that runs tests or migrations, a database per checkout.
The state file records the goal, the merge grant as 'no grant yet', and an empty Decisions log.
Every file the launch writes into a worktree (ORCHESTRATOR-BRIEF.md and claude-start.cmd) is covered by a `.git/info/exclude` entry, alongside the state file.
Staggers the two launches (about 30 seconds) and asks each session to report the name ListAgents shows for it.
